chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Usamah Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who does not find consolation in the Consolation of Allah, his soul will be cut off by regrets for the world; and the one who follows his gaze with what is in the hands of people, his worries will increase and his anger will not be satisfied; and the one who does not see a blessing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon him except in food or drink or clothing, then his deeds have been deficient and his punishment has drawn near.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual consequences of fixating on worldly possessions and limiting gratitude to physical needs?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on love of the world, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the spiritual pathology of *ghurm* (greed) by linking internal regret to external fixation. It warns that reducing divine grace (*ni'mah*) solely to material sustenance reflects a narrow worldview that hastens divine punishment, a concept central to Shia asceticism (*zuhd*). This triad of conditions serves as a diagnostic tool for evaluating the depth of one's faith and the quality of their deeds.
